newsitem.title: USA: US money managers bullish on US debt latest wk-MCM.
newsitem.headline: US money managers bullish on US debt latest wk-MCM.

text.p: Fixed-income managers remained bullish on U.S. debt in the week ended September 16, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

Money managers were convinced Federal Reserve policy makers would not raise interest rates this month, said the report, compiled before Tuesday morning, when a Fed source said eight regional Fed bank governors requested a rate hike.
"This is not your leveraged group, but instead is bullish and looking for ways to enhance yield," MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague said in comments attatched to the report.
"Spread product indications are that corporates are tight, and mortgages are a better bet," added McTeague, who conducts the weekly asset allocation survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 106.5 percent in the week ended September 16 from 106.1 percent in the prior week.

A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market. A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 15 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," down from 19 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" grew to 24 percent, up from 22 percent in the week ended September 9.
Sixty-one percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 56 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.79 percent, against 2.96 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 25 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 24 percent in the previous week, while 29 percent underweighted it. The remaining 46 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 36 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 16 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants, who manage about $90.0 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM.
